question: How many total medals did India win at the 2025 World Boxing Cup?
solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India won a total of **11 medals** at the **2025 World Boxing Cup**, a significant achievement in the international boxing arena.
 
• The tally of medals reflects India's growing prominence in the sport of boxing, with contributions from both male and female athletes across various weight categories.
 
• This success at the 2025 World Boxing Cup highlights the impact of improved training facilities, government initiatives, and support provided to Indian boxers in recent years.
 
• The medal count includes a mix of gold, silver, and bronze medals, showcasing the depth of talent in the Indian boxing contingent.
 
• India's performance at the event also aligns with its broader goal of excelling in global sports competitions and preparing for future events such as the Olympics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Boxing Cup:**

 
 
• The World Boxing Cup is an international boxing competition where athletes from various countries compete in different weight categories.
 
• It is organized by the **International Boxing Association (IBA)**, the governing body for amateur boxing worldwide.
 
• The event serves as a platform for showcasing emerging talent and fostering healthy competition among nations.
 
• It is held biennially and features both men’s and women’s events.
 
 
 
• **Indian Boxing Achievements:**
 
 
• India has consistently improved its performance in boxing over the years, with athletes winning medals in events like the Olympics, Asian Games, and World Championships.
 
• Prominent Indian boxers include **Mary Kom**, **Nikhat Zareen**, **Amit Panghal**, and **Lovlina Borgohain**, who have brought international acclaim to the country.
 
• Training centers such as the **National Boxing Academy** in Rohtak and the **Army Sports Institute** in Pune have played a key role in nurturing talent.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched schemes like **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** to provide financial and infrastructural support to athletes.
 
• Programs like **Khelo India** aim to identify and develop young sports talent in the country.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 2025 World Boxing Cup:**
 
 
• The event served as a preparatory ground for Indian boxers ahead of major competitions like the **2028 Summer Olympics**.
 
• India’s performance at the event boosted the morale of athletes and inspired upcoming boxers to pursue the sport professionally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Weight Categories:**

 
 
• In boxing, athletes compete in different weight divisions such as flyweight, lightweight, middleweight, and heavyweight.
 
• Each category has specific weight limits, and athletes must qualify within these limits to compete.
 
 
 
• **Scoring System:**
 
 
• Boxing matches are judged based on a scoring system where points are awarded for clean punches and defensive skills.
 
• The boxer with the highest points at the end of the match, or the one who achieves a knockout, is declared the winner.
 
 
 
• **Role of Coaches:**
 
 
• Coaches play a pivotal role in preparing boxers by developing their techniques, strategies, and mental strength.
 
• India has a growing pool of experienced boxing coaches, some of whom have international certifications.
